why: Fix round one for ticket 1067 in next/ and our tooling, after the review row 2026-11-15-t1067-review1: one agent wrote the laws and the fix (0177). Laws R14 to R17 went into next/packages/vitest/src/Recorder.types.test.ts and were red on the reviewed Recorder.ts in the package's own tsc before the fix. The fix, in next/packages/vitest/src/Recorder.ts: Args and Failure split over each method name; Method, Args and Failure read a member without its undefined; a service with an overloaded method does not compile as a Recorder layer; fails may name only a method impl gives, and impl may name only the service's own members. The pattern doc's claim and its line references were brought in line. Recorder.test.ts, Recorder.types.test.ts, Publish.test.ts, Queue.test.ts and the settings Command.test.ts are green one file at a time.
note: Overloads are refused, not supported: reading every overload needs a fixed-count pattern match with known quirks, while telling one signature from several takes one small type (its last two signatures, compared). A generic method is one signature and is not refused. layer gains a third type parameter, P, the type of impl, with a default, so fails can be held to impl's keys; P alone would lose the check on a misspelled impl key, so impl is also held to the service's keys through NoInfer, which keeps impl's lambdas contextually typed. watch is called as watch<S>, since S could no longer be inferred from impl's new type. The type-only law rule (0527) allows no call, so R16 and R17 read layer's parameters by explicit instantiation; the inferred path was checked once in a scratch file, removed.
